prerequisites: Strength of materials and solid mechanics course S5

learning_outcomes.text: Identify and analyze damage processes in composite materials and structures.
Understand and analyze the mechanical behavior of parts and structures in the presence of microscopic and macroscopic cracks.
Know the different damage mechanisms and how to measure them experimentally.
Be familiar with the consequences of damage and learn how to use a coupled microscopic-macroscopic approach to design composite structures under cyclic loading.
Be familiar with the main stress analysis results in the vicinity of a crack within the context of linear fracture mechanics.
Be familiar with the concepts of stress intensity factor and energy restitution rate.
Know the basic rules for dimensioning cracked parts based on the previous concepts.
Know how to perform a toughness characterization test.

syllabus_topics: Course 1: Fracture mechanics
Analysis of cracks in two-dimensional linear elasticity
Stress and displacement fields
Notion of stress intensity factor
Notion of toughness
Plastic analysis in the vicinity of a crack
Irwin's approach
Plastic zone correction and effective stress intensity factor
Experimental determination of toughness
Energy methods
Energy restitution rate (G)
Contour integrals (J)
Crack propagation
Bifurcation criteria and crack propagation laws
Course 2: Damage to composite materials
Damage processes: microscopic phenomena and macroscopic mechanical manifestations (property degradation, induced anisotropy, unilateral effect)
Damage mechanics: objectives, scale of study, general principles
Description of damage: microscopic (counting, defect density function) and macroscopic (physical properties, mechanical properties, notion of effective stress) approaches.

Lab 1: Development of experimental protocols based on scientific publications and associated standards to implement an approach for the design of composite structures under cyclic mechanical loading (tension, self-heating, fatigue).
Lab 2: Familiarization with and implementation of the experimental protocols to define the static mechanical behavior of the composite material and determine its elastic properties.
Definition of a fatigue cycle and acquisition of observable variables (force, displacement, temperature, number of cycles).
Lab 3: Post-processing and analysis of the obtained observable variables to determine the fatigue behavior of the stressed composite structure.
Highlighting the evolution of elastic properties over time and the progression of damage variables.

assessment_methods.method: DS1 (presumably a written exam or continuous assessment)

assessment_rules: The evaluation formula is (1.2*DS1 + 0.8*TP1)/2. The specific weighting percentages for DS1 and TP1 are not explicitly given as 100%, but rather as parts of a formula.
